name: Copy Number Variant
definition: A variation that increases or decreases the copy number of a given region.

name: Single Nucleotide Variant
definition: Single Nucleotide Variants (SNVs) are single nucleotide positions in genomic DNA at which different sequence alternatives exist.

name: Intron variant
definition: A transcript variant occurring within an intron.

name: Intergenic variant
definition: A sequence variant located in the intergenic region, between genes.

name: Splice site variant
definition: A sequence variant that changes the first two or last two bases of an intron, or the 5th base from the start of the intron in the orientation of the transcript.

name: 5' UTR variant
definition: A UTR variant of the 5' UTR.

name: 3' UTR variant
definition: A UTR variant of the 3' UTR.

name: Regulatory region variant
definition: A sequence variant located within a regulatory region.

name: Genic upstream transcript variant
definition: A variant that falls upstream of a transcript, but within the genic region of the gene due to alternately transcribed isoforms.

name: Synonymous variant
definition: A sequence variant where there is no resulting change to the encoded amino acid.

name: Non-synonymous variant
definition: A non-synonymous variant is an inframe, protein altering variant, resulting in a codon change.

name: MNV
definition: An MNV is a multiple nucleotide variant (substitution) in which the inserted sequence is the same length as the replaced sequence.

name: Insertion
definition: The sequence of one or more nucleotides added between two adjacent nucleotides in the sequence.

name: Deletion
definition: The point at which one or more contiguous nucleotides were excised.

name: Duplication
definition: An insertion which derives from, or is identical in sequence to, nucleotides present at a known location in the genome.

name: Inversion
definition: A continuous nucleotide sequence is inverted in the same position.

name: Translocation
definition: A region of nucleotide sequence that has translocated to a new position. The observed adjacency of two previously separated regions.
